title: What the text suggests about X
subtitle: Central Ideas and Details · 20 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **20 of the official questions in Central Ideas and Details are this one** — 2 Easy, 2 Medium, 16 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:

- The stem uses 'most strongly suggest', 'suggest', or 'can most reasonably be inferred' about something the passage describes indirectly, such as a conventional method set against a new one, a family presented through what locals say, or the implication of a controlled variable.
- Usually these are hard, with dense or ironic prose.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Find the contrast or framing: the new method is praised because the old one has a stated drawback, or a narrator reports what locals claim without endorsing it.
- 2) Put the implication in your own words, one step beyond what is literally said.
- 3) Pick the choice that is exactly that one step, not two.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: The text implies a limitation, and you pick a choice that claims something absolute (the old method doesn't work at all).
In literary texts, you miss the irony and take the locals' boasting as the narrator's own opinion.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
The text implies a limitation, and you pick a choice that claims something absolute (the old method doesn't work at all).
In literary texts, you miss the irony and take the locals' boasting as the narrator's own opinion.
